title: Milk soured with lemon juice for sour milk or buttermilk

evidence.basis: Knowledge packet 2026-10-13 item E2, PROPOSED (not approved). Research acidified_milk_for_buttermilk (SOURCE_SUPPORTED): King Arthur SRC-CM-26#a (1 tbsp acid stirred into 1 cup milk, stand 10-15 min; biscuits rose and browned like buttermilk ones, flavour flatter SRC-CM-26#b/#c); USU, NDSU, OSU, Illinois, NCSU, Land O'Lakes (1 tbsp acid with milk to make 1 cup, stand 5 min). Selected: King Arthur's proportion (the same volume of milk plus 1 tbsp lemon juice per cup), so the milk keeps the recipe's own cup measure. Conflicts kept: total volume (KA 1 cup + 1 tbsp vs others 1 cup) and stand time (5-15 min). Sour milk here: the research covers soured milk made this way; old recipes' naturally soured milk is the same job (acid for the soda). Not for dishes where buttermilk is the main flavour (KA), which this can't detect: stated in the tradeoff. Input bounds 1/2-4 cups are engineering bounds.

ops.text: Stir the lemon juice into the milk first and let it stand for about five minutes, until it thickens slightly, before you add it.

consequence.headline: Use milk soured with lemon juice instead.
consequence.reason: The baking soda needs an acid, and soured milk supplies it: a tablespoon of lemon juice in each cup of milk (King Arthur; extension guides use the same mix).
consequence.tradeoff: It rises and browns much the same but tastes a little flatter. Where the buttermilk's own flavour is the point, it isn't a match. Not kitchen-tested in this recipe.

proposal.text: Yes, if you sour the milk first with lemon juice.
